body:
## Summary
The rig's animation semantics - how the seam brightens with the voice, how an eye blinks as an iris or dims as a facet, how a float drifts, how far the aperture opens, how the gaze moves the eye light - are written out three times, once in each WebGL renderer (glow, cut, depth), along with three copies of texture upload, program build and context-loss rebuild. Pull the per-layer rules into one pure `layer-frame.ts` and the GL plumbing into `gl-kit.ts`; each renderer keeps only what is genuinely its own (its passes, its mesh, its composite).

## Description
Leans on talking-avatar / rig-parameter-contract: 'everything the renderer can derive on its own stays in the renderer' - but in ONE place - and 'each target renderer maps every channel or says it ignores it'. Today a new layer field (a brow, a third blink style, a voice-reactive halo) must be added in three files that already drift: the gaze channel has three different mappings (glow.ts:344, cut/renderer.ts:311, depth/renderer.ts:325) with nothing saying which differences are deliberate. Also module-design / seams-and-adapters ('two producers must feed one consumer identically; classify known divergences'): `layerFrame(draw, pose, rig, mapping)` returns plain numbers {skip, gain, eye, eyeP, gaze, float, aper}; each renderer passes a small mapping table (its gaze px, its follow rule) so the divergences become declared data instead of drifted code. Behaviour is pinned first by a recording fake WebGL2 context whose call streams are captured on the untouched tree.

## Flow
- Write the recording fake gl + goldens for all three renderers on the current tree (green).
- Write layer-frame tests (red), implement layer-frame.ts (green).
- gl-kit.ts: compileProgram (cut/gpu.ts program moves here), uploadLayerTextures, contextLossGuard.
- Switch glow, then cut, then depth, one commit each; the goldens stay byte-identical.

## Expected impact
Renderer files shrink by ~150 lines each; per-layer rules become testable without a GPU for the first time; the next renderer variant or rig channel is one edit, not three; gaze divergences become a reviewed table.

## Evaluation
Claim: the per-layer rules and GL plumbing exist once, with behaviour unchanged.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (layer-frame/gl-kit absent; the rg counts read 3; case 6 is a guard, green both sides)
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: glow.ts:325 `if (kind === 5) gain *= 0.9 + (l.voice_gain ?? 2) * Math.max(voice * 0.8, pose.open) * 0.6;` == cut/renderer.ts:298 == depth/renderer.ts:312. glow.ts:291 / cut/renderer.ts:272 / depth/renderer.ts:283 `const lift = ap ? pose.open * (ap.open_frac ?? 0.15) * (ap.bottom - ap.top) * (0.75 + 0.35 * Math.min(1, voice)) : 0;` (rg hit in 3 files). `gl.pixelStorei(gl.UNPACK_PREMULTIPLY_ALPHA_WEBGL, false)` at glow.ts:131, cut/renderer.ts:118, depth/renderer.ts:155. `addEventListener("webglcontextlost"` at glow.ts:249, cut/renderer.ts:234, depth/renderer.ts:242. `phase2: 2.3 * fi + 1.1` at glow.ts:196, cut/renderer.ts:176, depth/renderer.ts:201. u_gaze: glow.ts:344 `pose.gazeX * 3.5, pose.gazeY * 2.0`; cut/renderer.ts:311 `pose.gazeX * EYE_PX[0]`; depth/renderer.ts:325 `look.eyeX + pose.gazeX * 3.5`.

critic.reason: Real triplicated logic with documented drift, safe refactor plan behind golden call streams.

title: The shipped glow face never turns to the chatter it is answering
acceptance: lookBox(): subscribe(fn); set(LOOK_CHAT) -> fn called once with {x:1,y:-0.1}; set(LOOK_CHAT) again -> not called again; after unsubscribe, set(LOOK_HOST) -> not called

glow face loop (createDriver idleLinger 1 + withLook in glow units, hand clock) settled at rest, then look.set(LOOK_CHAT) -> loop.running true on the next tick, and after 0.6 s of ticks pose.yaw > 0.8 * GLOW_LOOK_YAW and pose.gazeX * 3.5 > 3 (px); before: startFace drops `look`, yaw stays the driver's drift
the same glow loop with no look change after settling -> hand clock scheduled false (the look adds no frames of its own)
glow face under calm (data-motion=calm), look.set(LOOK_CONTENT) -> exactly one still frame drawn with yaw = 0.6 * GLOW_LOOK_YAW and the loop not running

cut face with a look source (createCutRenderer mocked, WebGL2RenderingContext stubbed), driver settled and look unchanged -> shared clock size 0 and not scheduled; before: the per-frame look subscriber at cut/index.ts:136 keeps the clock scheduled forever

depth face with a look source (vi.useFakeTimers, createDepthRenderer + fetchDepth mocked) -> vi.getTimerCount() === 0 after start, and a look.set wakes the loop; before: a 100 ms setInterval is live for the face's lifetime
premise: apps/stage/src/Stage.tsx:116-118 - the stage computes where Malakor should look (lookFor: chat column while the caption answers chatters, content in corner layouts) every render
apps/stage/src/Stage.tsx:154 - and hands it to <Avatar look={look} variant={variant}>
apps/stage/src/source.ts:41-43 - the variant defaults to `glow` (anything but cut|depth is glow), so the broadcast runs the glow face

apps/stage/src/avatar/runtime.ts:143-152 - the glow startFace options have no `look`; apps/stage/src/avatar/variants.ts:25 adds `look` only to the type the other variants take - the shipped face ignores LOOK_CHAT and LOOK_CONTENT entirely
apps/stage/src/avatar/look.ts:26-33 - LookBox is get/set only: no event, so every consumer must poll
apps/stage/src/avatar/Avatar.tsx:58,62 - Avatar always passes a look source, so the cut and depth polling paths are always on

apps/stage/src/avatar/cut/index.ts:133-140 - cut subscribes `() => { if (driver.poll()) l.wake(); }` to the shared clock; it returns undefined, and apps/stage/src/avatar/motion.ts:52 drops a subscriber only on `false`, so the page's frame clock never idles with ?avatar=cut (contradicts runtime.ts:6-11 'none when nothing moves')
apps/stage/src/avatar/depth/index.ts:141-151 - depth polls the look with a 100 ms setInterval for the face's whole life

apps/stage/src/avatar/cut/look.ts:83-155 - a pure eyes-lead/head-follows look driver (withLook) already exists and is tested; its gaze is in cut units (EYE_PX 9/6, lines 23-24) and needs a units option to drive glow's 3.5/2 px eye light (glow.ts:344) without editing glow.ts
rollback: Three commits: (1) LookBox.subscribe + Avatar forwarding (additive), (2) glow runtime wraps its driver with withLook and wakes on the look event, (3) cut/depth replace polling with the event. Revert (2) alone to restore the old glow face; (1) and (3) stand on their own.

body:
## Summary
When Malakor answers a chatter, the stage already decides he should look at the chat column, and in a corner layout at the content (Stage.tsx:116-118). The face viewers actually see - the default `glow` variant - throws that away: its startFace takes no look (runtime.ts:143-152). Give the glow face the eyes-lead, head-follows look the cut-out prototype already has, and make the look an event instead of a poll, which also stops the cut face from keeping the page's frame clock running forever and the depth face from waking ten times a second.

## Description
Viewer-facing: a host who turns toward the person they are answering reads as listening to that person. The data exists, the behaviour is built (cut/look.ts withLook, tested), and the shipped face does not use it. Leans on talking-avatar / procedural-presence-motion (presence comes from motion that relates to what is happening) and face-signal-across-surfaces ('a face renderer threatens a window's idle cost': still at rest, woken by change, never polled). LookBox gains `subscribe` (fires only on a real change); Avatar forwards it through its look ref; glow's startFace wraps its driver with withLook (a `units` option keeps glow's 3.5/2 px saccades and adds the look on top, with a glow head-turn cap GLOW_LOOK_YAW ~6 deg so the orthographic warp does not tear) and wakes on the event; reduced motion snaps to the look in one still frame. cut and depth drop their per-frame subscriber and their setInterval for the same event.

## Flow
- look.ts: LookBox.subscribe; variants.ts: LookSource.subscribe optional.
- Avatar.tsx: the ref-backed look source forwards subscribe.
- runtime.ts: withLook(createDriver, look, glow units); look event -> loop.wake().
- cut/index.ts, depth/index.ts: event replaces poll; cut/look.ts gains the units option.
- Eyeball with `?face=demo` and a chat-answer caption on glow, then cut, then depth.

## Expected impact
On the default broadcast face Malakor turns to the chat column for every chat answer and toward the content in corner layouts; cut and depth return to zero frames and zero timers at rest.

## Evaluation
Claim: the glow face follows the stage's look, and no variant polls it.
Before: 0 of 6 acceptance cases pass (no LookBox event; glow ignores look; cut keeps the clock scheduled; depth holds a live interval)
After: 6 of 6
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: Stage.tsx:116-118 `const look = useMemo(() => lookBox(), []); const gaze = lookFor(scene.layout, speaking && caption ? caption.replyingTo : null); useEffect(() => look.set(gaze), [look, gaze]);` Stage.tsx:154 `<Avatar ... variant={variant} look={look} />`. source.ts:41-43 variantParam -> 'glow' unless cut|depth. runtime.ts:143-152 startFace(opts: {root, canvas, rigBase, source, size, clock?, onDrawn?}) - no look. variants.ts:25 `StartFaceOptions = Parameters<typeof glowStartFace>[0] & { look?: LookSource }`. cut/index.ts:136-138 `clock.subscribe(() => { if (driver.poll()) l.wake(); })` (returns undefined); motion.ts:52 `if (keep === false) subs.delete(fn); else subs.set(fn, time);` and :55 `if (subs.size > 0) schedule();`. depth/index.ts:144 `const poll = setInterval(() => {...}, 100);`. look.ts:26-33 lookBox has get/set only.

critic.reason: Strong, grounded, viewer-visible fix that also removes a never-idling clock and a perpetual timer.
